english: I am so proud of my daughter's success.
tip: The suffix '-yla' means with: 'başarısıyla' means with her success, one word doing the job of a preposition.

english: Even though it rained, the picnic was enjoyable.
tip: To say despite, use '-masına rağmen': 'yağmasına rağmen' means despite the fact that it rained.

english: We made the children drink milk.
tip: Adding '-ir' makes a verb causative: 'içmek' is to drink, so 'içirdik' means we made someone drink.

english: Hello, please come in.
tip: 'buyurun' is an all-purpose polite word for go ahead or help yourself. 'içeri buyurun' means please come in.

english: I decided on my own.
tip: 'kendi başıma' is a set phrase for on my own, by myself. Change 'başıma' to 'başına' for on your own.

english: Trash is collected every morning.
tip: The '-ır' ending on 'toplanır' marks a routine, not a one-off: trash gets collected regularly, every morning.

english: We should read to improve ourselves.
tip: The '-malı' in 'okumalıyız' marks necessity: we should read. Add '-malı' or '-meli' to any verb for must or should.

english: When the storm hit, I opened the window.
tip: The '-ınca' on 'çıkınca' means when or as soon as. It attaches to the verb, so Turkish needs no separate word for when.

english: The film lasted two and a half hours.
tip: 'buçuk' means and a half after a number: 'iki buçuk saat' is two and a half hours.

english: When I woke up in the morning the sun had already risen.
tip: The '-muştu' on 'doğmuştu' is the past perfect: the sun had already risen before another past moment.

english: The thief was caught by the police.
tip: In a passive sentence, 'tarafından' marks the doer: 'polis tarafından yakalandı' is was caught by the police.

english: My condolences, I am very sorry.
tip: 'başınız sağ olsun' is the set condolence phrase, literally may your head stay well. Used only to offer sympathy.

english: We waited for the boss to find a nurse.
tip: 'bulsun' (let him find) plus 'diye' means so that: 'bulsun diye bekledik' is we waited so that he would find one.

english: If I had charged my phone, I could call now.
tip: The '-seydim' in 'etseydim' marks an unreal if: 'şarj etseydim' means if I had charged it, implying I did not.

target: Ramazan ayında oruç tutmak maneviyatı güçlendirir.
english: Fasting during Ramadan strengthens spirituality.
tip: To fast is 'oruç tutmak', literally to hold a fast. Turkish pairs 'oruç' with 'tutmak', hold, not a single verb.

english: My mother made me walk to school.
tip: 'yürüttü' is causative: 'yürü-' (walk) plus '-t' means made someone walk. Add '-t' or '-dır' to a verb to say you made someone do it.

english: When the weather warmed up, I ran home.
tip: '-ınca' means when or once: 'ısın-' (warm up) plus '-ınca' gives 'ısınınca', once it warmed up. No separate word for when is needed.

english: I do laundry twice a week.
tip: For how often, the time unit takes '-da': 'haftada iki kez' means twice a week, with '-da' carrying the sense of per.

english: I will be there in twenty minutes.
tip: 'içinde' after a time span means within: 'yirmi dakika içinde' is within twenty minutes. The noun before it stays plain, no case ending.

english: I waited half an hour, nobody came.
tip: 'kimse' (nobody) needs a negative verb: 'kimse gelmedi' means nobody came. Turkish doubles the negative, 'kimse' plus '-me' on the verb.

target: Bu ayakkabıları çok beğendim ama pahalı.
english: I really liked these shoes but they're expensive.
tip: 'beğenmek' (to like) takes a marked object: 'ayakkabıları çok beğendim', I really liked the shoes, marked by '-ı' on 'ayakkabıları'.

target: Düz gidin, ikinci sokaktan sola dönün.
english: Go straight, turn left at the second street.
tip: Turning toward something uses '-a/-e': 'sol' (left) becomes 'sola' in 'sola dönün', turn to the left.

target: O bugün film izledi ama pek beğenmedi.
english: He watched a movie today but didn't really like it.
tip: 'pek' before a negative means not really: 'pek beğenmedi' is didn't really like it. 'pek' needs the negative verb to carry this sense.

target: Elli lira yeter mi, yoksa daha fazla mı lazım?
english: Is fifty lira enough, or do we need more?
tip: 'yoksa' joins two choices in a question as or: 'yeter mi, yoksa daha fazla mı' is it enough or is more needed. Each choice keeps its 'mı'.

english: We had our house painted by the painter.
tip: When you have someone do a job, the doer takes '-a/-e': 'boyacıya' with 'boyattık' means we had the painter paint it for us.

english: Dear director, I would like to present my report.
tip: 'Sayın' before a name or title is a formal Dear or Esteemed: 'Sayın müdürüm' opens a polite or written address to a director.

target: Önce soğanları doğrarsın, sonra yağda kavurursun.
english: First you chop the onions, then fry them in oil.
tip: 'önce' ... 'sonra' frames a sequence as first ... then: 'önce soğanları doğrarsın, sonra kavurursun', first you chop, then you fry.

target: Seksen yaşında bir dede bize yol gösterdi.
english: An eighty-year-old grandfather showed us the way.
tip: For age, add '-ında' to 'yaş': 'seksen yaşında' means eighty years old, literally at the age of eighty.

target: Üç kilo domates ve iki kilo soğan aldım.
english: I bought three kilos of tomatoes and two kilos of onions.
tip: After a number the noun stays singular: 'üç kilo domates', three kilos of tomato, never 'domatesler'. No plural '-ler' follows a count.

target: Zeynep her pazar alışveriş merkezine gitse de bu sefer evde kalmayı tercih etti.
english: Even though Zeynep goes to the shopping mall every Sunday, this time she preferred to stay home.
tip: '-se de' on a verb means even though: 'gitse de' means even though she goes, though she goes there regularly.
